# Zhex

> Zhex is a Forth-inspired programming language for builders, built on small words and big ideas: you build the vocabulary you program with, and every word you write extends the language. Compact code with visible flow, meaningful names, and checked types, executed by a working Go interpreter. Every program is checked — names, types, and word connections — before any of it runs.

## Docs

- [Manifesto](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/manifesto.html): the intentions behind Zhex — visible data, small composed words, a language machines can read, errors that teach, performance you can measure, and code humans enjoy reviewing. Full text at docs/manifesto.md; concrete goals at docs/language-goals.md.
- [Docs](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/tldr.html): the TL;DR-first guide — Zhex in a minute, then topic pages for language concepts, the standard library, and tools.
- [Getting started](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/getting-started.html): install and run a first program.
- Agent workflow: write the program, then run `zhex run file.zhex --report=json` — checking happens before execution, so a clean run means names, types, and word connections resolved. Read each report entry `{code, severity, file, line, column, message, hint}` (plus the additive `span_start_column`/`span_end_column` on checker diagnostics and `url` on catalog codes) and fix what it names; the hint states the action, and human-readable diagnostics show the source line with a caret under the whole failing expression. Rerun until clean. When a report names a code, `zhex errors <code>` prints that code's full catalog entry — meaning and fix plus its learn URL — offline from inside the binary (`zhex errors` lists every code, `zhex errors --json` emits the catalog as JSON, and an unknown code suggests the closest). To watch what a program did instead, add `--trace` — JSONL step events stream to stderr before any diagnostic, tracing never fails a run, and the flags combine (events, then the report). To compile a checked program instead of interpreting it, run `zhex compile file.zhex [-o out] [--target=browser|wasi|native]`. The WebAssembly targets (browser is the default) assemble with the free wasm-tools tool — install it with `cargo install wasm-tools`, `pacman -S wasm-tools`, or `brew install wasm-tools` (a release binary from the BytecodeAlliance releases page also works), and without it the coded `missing-tool` diagnostic prints those three install lines. The native target emits a self-contained, readable Go program directory (main.go, go.mod, zhexrt runtime sources), builds it with the Go toolchain when Go is present (otherwise it writes the sources with the one `go build` instruction), keeps the interpreter's full 128-bit integers, and fences generic choices, json.decode, xml.decode, the temporal words, file.free-space, error.set-reporter, constructor partials, recursive word defaults, checked indexed writes, and fallible callbacks. A construct the target does not cover yet fails the compile with `not-available-in-build` naming the construct — run that program with `zhex run` instead. Native binaries measure a 10.6x geometric-mean speedup over the interpreter across the benchmark workloads (docs/measurements.md in the repository). Explore interactively by piping entries to `zhex repl` standard input — words and values persist across entries, `words` lists effective signatures, and an error prints its diagnostic while the session survives. Take example code and output from the examples page — both come from the actual interpreter.
- [Language](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/syntax.html): syntax, values, words, flows, control flow, Results, and modules.
- What Zhex does not have: no method syntax — a dot qualifies a word name (`text.upper(s)`) or reads a record field (`customer.name`), never a method call (field and indexed reads do chain in one postfix expression, `space.bytes[i].x`); no lambda or anonymous functions — callbacks are named words or partials built from `_` holes; no generic words or records — only choices and `Option<T>` take a type parameter; no iterator or lazy-sequence values — iteration exists only as `for ... in` loops (range, list, array, map, file.stream) and `while`; no string interpolation — concatenate with `+` (a String and an Int concatenate; two Ints add) and convert with `int.to-string`; no exceptions — failures are `Result` values handled with postfix `try` or `catch` at every caller; no `break`, `continue`, or early `return` — a word's value is its final expression, and an `if`, `match`, or `flow` block can supply it conditionally; chained branches use `elif`; no null — absence is `Option.None`; no implicit conversions except the string-context Int for `+` and `print`; no compound assignment — write `count = count + 1`; conditions must be `Bool`, never numbers or strings.
- Block values: `if`, `match`, and `flow` can be the entire right-hand side of a `let`, `var`, or assignment; the block's final value is used, and a `with` continuation under the seed line composes the same way. They are not general nested expressions or call arguments. With blocks: `with <namespace>` directly under a `flow` seed line (same indentation, no blank or comment line between) fixes the seed — every step receives the original seed as its first argument, never the previous step's result; bare step names resolve through the namespace first (`append` under `with list` is `list.append`), then as ordinary words with the seed; the last step's value is the block's value; the namespace is built-in or a used module; a step resolving nowhere fails `with-step` naming both tries, a `Result` seed must be handled first, a Unit seed fails `with-seed`, and an unfusable `with` line fails `with-location`. The `flow` keyword may be dropped exactly on the seed line above `with` (a fused `let`/`var`/assignment right-hand side receives the block's value); a naked expression elsewhere stays a discarded no-op, `with` is a reserved keyword, and the REPL takes the explicit `flow` form.
- While loops: `while condition` repeats an indented body while its `Bool` condition holds, evaluated before each pass. It is a statement of type `Unit` — never a binding or assignment right-hand side — with no `break`/`continue`; it may run forever by design with no iteration limit, and the word-call depth limit does not apply to loop iterations.
- Multiline syntax: expressions may continue inside `()`, `[]`, and `{}`; blank and comment-only lines are allowed while a delimiter is open. Trailing commas are rejected, and `<...>` type arguments do not open a continuation.
- Word doc comments: a contiguous block of full-line `##` comments at column 1 directly above a `word` declaration becomes that word's doc — one optional leading space is stripped per line, lines join with newlines, a blank line or plain `#` comment between the block and `word` detaches it, and `##` anywhere else stays a plain comment (`###` reads as `##` plus text). User words only: entry-file words, module words (`words` lists them qualified, e.g. `math.gcd(...)`), and REPL definitions; records, choices, and built-ins get none. `words` prints the doc indented four spaces beneath the signature, a blank doc line as an empty line; docs live on the word, so a redefinition replaces the doc and a doc-less redefinition clears it without affecting signature compatibility. In the REPL, a comment-only line never completes an entry — it joins the next line's entry (a `##` doc block shares its entry with the word it documents), and `words` typed right after a comment line still runs the command.
- Simple word calls and partials: parenthesized calls remain valid; a simple call may omit call parentheses at a complete statement, binding/assignment right-hand side, final word value, or flow step. Commas separate arguments (`add 1, 2`); whitespace alone does not. `print 1 + 1` passes one arithmetic result. Keep nested calls parenthesized (`print(add(1, 2))`) and use parentheses for negative or list-literal first arguments; `values [0]` remains indexing. A bare word name at a complete expression boundary calls an accessible zero-argument word, while a same-named value binding is a value. A flow step receives the current value as its first argument, then any comma-separated extra arguments. A trailing `try` or `catch` guards the whole bare call; use parentheses to place `try` or `catch` on a fallible argument separately. A standalone `_` slot creates an explicit function value with required parameters in hole order. Supported built-ins and user words can be partially applied; overloaded built-ins need an annotation or sufficient call-site constraints, while constructors, loop-only operations, `error.set-reporter`, `console.exit`, and `console.fail` are excluded. Captured arguments evaluate once in source order at creation; defaults remain deferred until invocation. A fallible target's function type includes `Result` in its return and fails only when invoked; a capture-argument `try` happens at creation. Function values have monomorphic arrow types such as `(Int) -> Int` and do not enable automatic currying.
- [Calls and defaults](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/calls.html): simple comma-separated word-call syntax, zero-argument calls, flow arguments, and boundaries where parentheses remain necessary.
- [Records and named types](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/records.html): nominal record declarations, positional or named construction, field defaults, immutable fields, and explicit type annotations.
- [Choices and matching](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/choices.html): concrete named alternatives, payload binding, exhaustive cases, and a final `case _` default.
- [Lists and arrays](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/collections.html): homogeneous shared collections, checked indexing, resizing, limits, and failure handling.
- [Maps](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/maps.html): typed inferred keys and values, `Option` lookup, insertion-ordered iteration, updates, and flows.
- [Dates and time zones](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/temporal.html): calendar dates, elapsed durations, instants, named IANA zones, and DST-aware operations.
- [JSON](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/json.html): typed JSON decoding with record defaults, strict validation and field paths, and encoding of supported values.
- [XML](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/xml.html): typed XML decoding with attribute fields, repeated-element lists, strict validation, element paths, and the common Error family.
- [Collection iteration](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/iteration.html): list indices, array coordinates, row-major arrays, insertion-ordered map traversal, and mutation guards.
- Rich-value rules: record declarations and choices are nominal. Record constructors accept all-positional arguments in field order or all-named arguments in any field order; the forms cannot mix. Trailing defaults may be omitted, and evaluate after supplied arguments in declaration order. Named arguments apply only to record constructors, not words, built-ins, or choice alternatives. `type Names = alias List<String>` defines a transparent alias. Fields are immutable; choice alternatives are constructed by qualified name, with payloads in declared order. A choice may have one type parameter: payload constructors infer it, while a nullary alternative needs an expected type. Generic records and words are not supported. Match every alternative once, or use one final `case _`; a default after all named alternatives is an error. Choices cannot be printed or compared directly, payloads cannot contain `Result`, and caught concrete errors need `error.wrap` before storing in an `Error` payload. Lists infer homogeneous elements; empty list values need an expected `List<T>`. Arrays use explicit `List<Int>` shapes, rank 1..32, and at most 1,000,000 elements. Mutation words return their receiver (`list.append`, `list.insert`, `array.resize`, `map.put`, `map.remove`, `map.into`, `buffer.add-line`, `buffer.set-line` each return the collection they mutated, so flows thread them). List/array reads, `array.new`, `list.append`, `list.insert`, and `array.resize` return ordinary values and diagnose invalid operations at runtime; direct `try` or `catch` selects a checked Result for that operation only. Plain indexed writes return `Unit` and raise runtime diagnostics for invalid rank, bounds, or active-iteration mutation; parenthesized indexed writes return a checked `Result<Unit, Error>`. `Map<K, V>` infers types from nonempty literals; empty maps need an expected type. Map literal keys are constant `String`, `Int`, or `Bool` literals; dynamic keys are allowed for lookup, update, containment, and removal. Lookup yields `Option<V>` without `try`, and map values cannot contain `Result`. Map iteration preserves insertion order. Mutation of an actively traversed map raises a runtime `collection-iterating` diagnostic before changing storage; it is not a `Result`. Collection aliases share storage. Caught concrete errors may go directly to built-in `error.*` operations, but require `error.wrap` before passing to a user word expecting `Error` or storing in an Error-typed record field or collection; flow cannot pass Error values to user-defined steps.
- [Standard library](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/text.html): text, buffers, files, and console operations.
- JSON: `json.decode(raw, defaults)` infers the target from a typed default and returns `Result<T, Error>`; missing record fields use defaults, invalid supplied fields do not. Present Lists/Maps replace defaults, and each decoded value gets fresh copies of mutable defaults while aliases inside that value remain shared. `json.encode(value)` returns compact JSON; record fields follow declaration order and Map keys follow insertion order. Supported types are `Int`, `Bool`, `String`, records, `List<T>`, `Map<String, T>`, and `Option<T>` in nested combinations, except direct nested `Option<Option<T>>`; `null` means `Option.None`. Int accepts signed 128-bit integer-form JSON tokens only; decimal/exponent notation and overflow reject. `json.parse(raw)` returns `Result<Json, Error>` — a host-predeclared recursive tree type `Json` with constructors `Json.Null`, `Json.Bool(value)`, `Json.Text(value)`, `Json.Number(literal: String)`, `Json.List(values: List<Json>)`, and `Json.Object(fields: Map<String, Json>)`; trees are ordinary data (constructible, storable in records, matched with plain `match`) and `json.encode(tree)` accepts them: `encode(parse(raw))` preserves key order and number literals byte-for-byte and normalizes whitespace to compact; `Json.Number` literals are validated against the JSON number grammar at encode (`json-type` plus a JSON Pointer path), `text.to-int` converts when an Int is wanted, and map lookup distinguishes `Option.Some(Json.Null)` from `Option.None`; recursion stays host-only (a user record may hold a `Json` field), JSON depth and word-call depth are both 256 so a recursive word over a maximally deep tree sits exactly at the call-depth edge. Arrays, resources, Results, non-Option choices, and non-string-key maps are unsupported. JSON errors include `json-syntax`, `json-type`, `json-field`, `json-range`, and `json-depth`; `error.detail(error, "path")` is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer, with root as empty string and `~`/`/` escaped as `~0`/`~1`.
- XML: `xml.decode(text, defaults)` infers the target from a typed default and returns `Result<T, Error>`, schema-directed exactly like `json.decode` (same supported types: `Int`, `Bool`, `String`, records, `List<T>`, `Map<String, T>`, `Option<T>` in nested combinations, except direct nested `Option<Option<T>>`). Mapping: element attributes map onto same-named record fields verbatim alongside child-element fields, and an attribute name colliding with a child element name fails the decode; repeated same-named child elements collect into a `List<T>` field in document order; an absent element or attribute falls back to its default (so `Option.None` default plus absence yields `Option.None`, and a present element yields `Option.Some`); text-only elements decode as `String` or `Int` (`Bool` accepts exactly `true`/`false`); for a `List` or `Map` target the element children are the items, keyed by child element name for maps. Strictness: unknown elements and attributes fail, duplicate non-list elements fail, missing required fields without defaults fail, mixed content (non-whitespace text next to child elements) fails, namespace-prefixed or namespace-resolved names fail (including a default `xmlns`), DTD/entity declarations and undefined entities fail, and malformed XML fails — all before any substitution. Entities: the five predefined (`&amp;` `&lt;` `&gt;` `&quot;` `&apos;`) and numeric character references decode; nothing is fetched, ever. Limits: nesting depth 256, one million elements. Errors are the common `Error` family with stable codes `xml-syntax`, `xml-type`, `xml-field`, `xml-range`, and `xml-depth`; `error.detail(error, "path")` carries the element path (`/server/endpoints/0/host`, root as empty string), plus `reason` (`unknown`, `duplicate`, `missing`, `collision`, `prefixed`), `expected`/`actual`, and `offset`/`line`/`column` for syntax failures.
- [Tools](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/repl.html): the REPL, diagnostics, compiling to WebAssembly and native Go, and editor support.
- Vocabulary: text work uses the `text.*` words — `length` (code points), `line-count`, `word-count`, `upper`, `lower`, `trim`, `contains`, `index-of` (code-point position, `-1` when absent), `slice(start, end)` (code points, bounds clamp, `start >= end` is empty), `replace(old, new)` (every occurrence, literal, empty `old` errors), `split(separator)` (literal, preserves empty fields, no trim, empty separator yields code points, fails `collection-limit` past one million elements), `join(separator)` (between elements, empty list is empty text), `to-code-points()` (the code points as a fresh `List<Int>` in order, fails `collection-limit` past one million elements), `from-code-points(list)` (rebuilds text; a code point that is not valid Unicode — negative, above U+10FFFF, or a surrogate half — fails `text-code-point`), `starts-with(prefix)` and `ends-with(suffix)` (literal, empty prefix/suffix matches), `repeat(n)` (n concatenated copies; count 0 is empty text, a negative count — or one whose result is longer than the runtime can allocate — fails `text-repeat-count`), `pad-left(width, fill = " ")` and `pad-right(width, fill = " ")` (pad to width in code points with a one-code-point fill defaulting to a space — an empty or multi-code-point fill fails `text-pad-fill`, a negative width fails `text-pad-width`, a width whose result is longer than the runtime can allocate fails `text-pad-width` too, and a width at or below the text's length returns it unchanged, padding never truncates), `wrap(width)` (greedy `List<String>` wrap on spaces with empty fields skipped: a line breaks before the first word that no longer fits, an over-long word overflows alone, empty or spaces-only input wraps to one empty line, width counts code points as a monospace approximation, and the one-million-line bound fails `collection-limit` before materializing), `insert(index, inserted)` (insertion points 0..length inclusive, index == length appends, out-of-range indexes clamp into range like `text.slice`), `remove(start, end)` (slice's mirror: the same clamped half-open range removed, an empty or inverted range is a no-op), and `sentences()` (the sentence layer as a `List<String>`: a run of the terminators `. ! ?`, optional closing quotes/brackets `" ' ” ’ ) ]`, then whitespace or the end; consecutive terminators stay together, each sentence keeps its punctuation and closers, the whitespace between sentences is dropped, empty or whitespace-only input is an empty list, and a final stretch without a terminator is its own sentence — so `text.join(sentences, " ")` restores a single-space text exactly; the rule has no abbreviation list, so `Dr.` and `e.g.` split; the one-million-sentence bound fails `collection-limit` before materializing), plus the earlier `reverse` and `to-int`. The no-implicit-conversions law has one exception — the string-context Int exception: `+` concatenates when exactly one operand is `Int` and the other is `String` (the Int renders as `int.to-string` does, chains associate left to right, and two `Int` operands still add numerically), and `print` accepts an `Int` directly; `Bool` and every other type stay strict in these positions, and no other position converts. Lists compose through callback words taking ordinary function values: `list.map(values, transform)` (once per element left to right, fresh outer list, shared elements, source unchanged), `list.filter(values, predicate)` (keep matches), `list.select(values, predicate)` (keep the matches unmodified; visits every element, never short-circuits), `list.fold(values, initial, step)` (returns the final accumulator), `list.find(values, predicate)` (`Option.Some` first match or `Option.None`, empty list is `None`), `list.any(values, predicate)` (short-circuits `true` at the first match, empty is `false`), `list.all(values, predicate)` (short-circuits `false` at the first non-match, empty is `true`), `list.sort(values)` (stable ascending copy of `List<Int>`/`List<String>`, code-point string order, fresh outer list, source unchanged), and `list.sort-by(values, key)` (stable ascending copy ordered by an Int-or-String key callback evaluated once per element in source order before sorting); membership answers directly — `list.contains(values, item)` accepts `List<Int>`/`List<String>` under `list.sort`'s constrained overloads, scans linearly to the first equal element holding the traversal guard, and an empty list is `false`; `list.insert(values, index, value)` places `value` at the zero-based insertion point `index` (`0` through the length inclusive, so index == length appends; anything else fails `list-range`) and returns the list it grew with `list.append`'s iteration-guard and element-limit rules, `try`/`catch` selecting the checked `Result<List<T>, Error>`; callbacks are explicit or word-name partials with no lambda syntax, may print or mutate unrelated values, cannot return a `Result` nor use one as a fold accumulator (`unhandled-result`), and the source list holds its `collection-iterating` traversal guard throughout. Arrays select whole rows: `array.select(values, predicate)` passes each row of a rank-2 array left to right as a fresh `List<T>`, keeps the rows whose `(List<T>) -> Bool` predicate holds unmodified (rectangle preserved, fresh outer array, zero rows when nothing matches), holds the source's traversal guard, and reports any rank besides 2 at runtime with `array.select requires a rank-2 array, found rank N` under the `array-rank` code. Lines build in a `Buffer`: `buffer.new()`, `buffer.add-line`, `buffer.line-count`, `buffer.line(i)` and `buffer.set-line(i, text)` (Results failing `buffer-range` on a bad index), `buffer.to-text`; `let` binds the buffer's name — two names observe one buffer — and `Buffer` is excluded from `==` and rejected by `print` (convert with `buffer.to-text`). Files read whole (`file.read(path)` to String) or streamed (`file.open(path)`, `file.read-line(f)` where end of file fails inside the Result, `file.close(f)` idempotent); `for line in file.stream(path)` streams chomped lines and guarantees the close on every exit, including loop-body failures. `file.write(contents, path, append = false)` writes text — contents first, then path; omitting `append` (or `false`) creates or truncates, `true` appends and creates a missing file; the trailing argument is a built-in constant default (calls may omit it, partials keep it deferred), no parent directory is created, the write is not atomic (a failure can leave a partial or truncated file), and the open/write/close stays inside the operation (no writable File escapes; created files 0644 before umask; symlinks followed). `file.write-bytes(path, bytes)` writes binary — path first, then a `List<Int>` of one byte per `Int` 0..255 (the first value outside that range fails `file-bytes-range` inside the Result before the file is opened; there is no append mode, no byte read, and no byte type; it shares file.write's create-or-truncate, mode, and phase rules). Path inspection: `file.list(folder)` returns a fresh `List<String>` of one folder level's bare entry names (not paths) in sorted order, dot entries included, inside `Result<List<String>, FileError>`, failing the shared `collection-limit` past one million entries before materializing; `file.exists(path)` is a plain `Bool` where a missing path is `false` and any other stat failure is a runtime diagnostic, with `try`/`catch` selecting the checked `Result<Bool, FileError>` form; `file.size(path)` returns a regular file's bytes (directories report `0`, no recursion) inside `Result<Int, FileError>`; `file.free-space(path)` accepts any existing path, file or folder, and returns the bytes available on its volume inside `Result<Int, FileError>` (Unix and Windows; other platforms fail inside the Result). Lexical path words compose and decompose without touching the disk, returning plain `String` (no Result, no `try`/`catch`): `file.join(base, child)` concatenates with the native separator and cleans (`..` resolves lexically, no containment guarantee) and an absolute child replaces the base (`file.join("a/b", "/c")` → `/c`); `file.base(path)` is the final element (trailing separators removed, the root is its own base, the empty path yields `.`); `file.extension(path)` is the final element's final-dot suffix including the dot (`.gz` for `report.tar.gz`, `.bashrc` for the dotfile, empty when absent); `file.directory-of(path)` drops the final element (a trailing separator leaves nothing to drop, the root is its own directory, no-drop yields `.`). Destructive operations return `Result<Unit, FileError>` with the same taxonomy: `file.make-folder(path, parents = false)` creates one folder level and fails on an existing target, while `parents = true` creates missing ancestors and tolerates an existing folder; `file.delete(path)` removes a file or an empty folder and fails on a nonempty one; `file.delete-folder(path, recursive = false)` removes an empty folder, and `recursive = true` removes the whole tree best-effort (part may be gone before the first failure; earlier effects stand); `file.move(source, target, overwrite = false)` is rename-based and moves folders as well as files, `overwrite = true` replaces an existing file only (folder targets are refused in both modes), cross-device moves fail with the platform's error with no copy fallback, and the target check and rename have a documented check-then-act window. File Results fail `file-open`, `file-read`, `file-write`, `file-bytes-range`, `file-utf8`, `file-list`, `file-exists`, `file-size`, `file-free-space`, `file-make-folder`, `file-delete`, `file-delete-folder`, or `file-move`, naming the path and the operating system's reason (`file-write` also names the failing phase: open, write, or close). Program arguments forward as `zhex run file.zhex [args...]`: read them with `console.args-count()` and `console.arg(i)` (a Result failing `argument-missing` on a bad index). Environment configuration reads the process environment: `env.get(name)` is a total `Option<String>` (unset is `Option.None`, set-but-empty is `Option.Some("")`; never a Result) and `env.load(path = ".env")` returns `Result<Unit, Error>` (common-Error family, the `json.parse` precedent), reading KEY=VALUE lines into the environment with first assignment wins — a key already in the environment, or set by an earlier line of the same file, is never overridden; blank lines and whole-line `#` comments are skipped after leading trim, one matching pair of surrounding single or double quotes on the value is stripped, `KEY=` sets the empty string, a read failure fails `env-read` and a malformed line (missing `=`, empty key, key with spaces) fails `env-parse` naming the line number, lines before a malformed one stay applied, and the `.env` trailing constant default stays deferred for partials like `file.write`'s `append`.
- Results and errors: built-ins return explicit `Result<T, E>`. Word parameter annotations may be omitted when body and same-program call constraints determine one concrete type; unresolved parameters need annotations, conflicting calls are type errors, and `Result` cannot be a word parameter. Trailing word parameters may have defaults; required parameters come first and calls remain positional. Defaults can infer parameter types, run lazily only when omitted, and evaluate after supplied arguments (source order) in parameter order. They use declaring-module scope, cannot reference parameters/globals/caller bindings or let a `Result` escape, and are fresh on each call; `words` displays `= ...`. Compatible REPL redefinitions affect new entries while checked callers retain the earlier word/defaults. Return annotations may also be omitted when the body determines one concrete success type. An escaping `try` infers one error family and the effective Result signature, and successful values are wrapped once. Pure words keep their inferred or annotated type. A recursive cycle without a concrete type anchor, empty collection, or nullary `Option.None` needs a return annotation. Explicit `Result<T, E>` signatures remain supported with `ok`/`err`, without wrapping twice. Each caller still uses `try` or `catch`; multiple uncaught families in one word are rejected, so catch a failure or explicitly wrap it as common `Error`. Runtime faults are not inferred. `catch [name]` lazily supplies a same-typed fallback or exits via `console.exit`/`console.fail`; the one-line fallback also binds on assignment right-hand sides and inside call arguments at expression boundaries, a trailing ungrouped catch on a short-form call's last argument guarding the whole call (the trailing-try rule), while block forms stay statement-only. Bare Results cannot be discarded; a stored `let pending = call()` must be handled by the immediately following same-block statement as exactly `pending try` or `pending catch ...`, standalone or as a whole new `let` RHS. Explicit flow steps use `word-name try`. `error.new` creates a cause-less application Error; `error.wrap` converts to common `Error` and preserves the cause; accessors include code/message/operation/file/line/column/detail/has-cause/cause. File detail `reason` values are `not-found`, `permission-denied`, `other` (open, write, and inspect), and `invalid-utf8`, `closed`, `read-failed`, `end-of-file` (read); a write failure's `detail` also carries its `phase`. `error.set-reporter(named-word)` installs a top-level `(Error) -> Unit` callback. `error.report(problem)` reports a handled occurrence; a failure escaping the program calls the reporter once before the diagnostic. Intermediate propagation does not report, duplicate occurrences are suppressed, callback failure/recursion is isolated, and no external destination is configured by default. `console.exit(status)` ends execution with 0..255, and `console.fail(message)` writes to stderr and ends with status 1; neither reports a valid deliberate exit. Out-of-range exit status is a runtime diagnostic. These exits close active `file.stream` loops; explicitly opened files still require `file.close`. Reporter calls to either operation cannot replace the original outcome.
- Modules: split a program across files with `use math` — it loads the sibling `math.zhex` next to the importing file (each file's own imports resolve beside it; the REPL resolves against the working directory and adopts the module for the session). Imported words are called qualified (`math.gcd(a, b)`); module words call each other bare inside their own file and cannot see the importer's words; a module's own imports stay private to it, and two modules never collide. A leading underscore makes a word or type module-private: calling one from outside fails `private-use`, and it is never suggested cross-module. A public signature, record field, or choice payload cannot expose a private type, even through a List, Array, Map, or Result. Imported choice constructors and cases are qualified (`model.Status.Ready`). Errors: a missing module fails `use-missing` naming the searched path; import cycles fail `use-cycle` spelling the files; module names `text`, `int`, `buffer`, `file`, `console`, `error`, `list`, `array`, `map`, `json`, `xml`, and `env` fail `use-reserved`; the built-in `Option` type and constructors are reserved names, but `Option` is not a reserved module name. Imported files may declare words and types but top-level statements fail `module-body`; the reserved zero-argument `main` word lets one file serve both roles — when an entry file's top level has no statements, `zhex run` and `zhex compile` invoke its `word main` automatically (parameters fail `main-parameters`; a failing Result inside reports like a top-level `try`), while a `main` beside top-level statements, in a module, or in the REPL stays an ordinary word; `use` outside a file's top level fails `use-location` — and `use` is a reserved word. Loaded modules check before their importers, and module errors annotate the module's own source. Trace events carry qualified names (`{"word":"math.gcd"}`, module-private words included) with word returns pointing into the module file (`{"file":"math.zhex"}`). Corpus examples: `examples/modules/main.zhex` (math) and `examples/modules/md-report/main.zhex` (a pure-Zhex Markdown report module with `md.heading`, `md.paragraph`, `md.bullet-list`, `md.ordered-list`, `md.link`, `md.code-block`, and `md.table` — fragment-returning words with per-position escaping, `max(3, longest run + 1)` fences, strict header-width table rows, and neutralized `javascript:`/`data:` link schemes), each a two-file program run as `zhex run examples/<path>`.
- [Examples](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/examples.html): runnable programs with source, sample input, and real output — the source and output on the page are produced by the actual interpreter. The 23 in-subset examples also run in the visitor's browser — the build precompiles each to a WebAssembly artifact (WebAssembly garbage collection: roughly Chrome 119+, Firefox 120+, Safari 18.2+) that a page shim executes with the Go interpreter's byte-for-byte output, while the other 24 stay fenced with notes naming the construct the compiler does not cover yet. `text-stats` is the first real application: run it as `zhex run examples/text-stats.zhex <file> [upper]` — one argument reports the file's line, word, and character counts from one whole read, and any second argument streams the file uppercased line by line. `file-work` is the destructive round trip: run it as `zhex run examples/file-work.zhex <folder>` — it creates a zhex-work folder under the argument, writes and inspects two reports, and removes the tree. `env-config` is the configuration round trip: run it as `zhex run examples/env-config.zhex <folder>` — it writes a report.env fixture, loads it with first assignment wins, and reads each setting back through `env.get` Option matches. `collatz` shows the while loop: run it as `zhex run examples/collatz.zhex` — it prints each number's steps to reach 1, ending by its condition rather than a bound.
- [Demos](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/demos.html): Zhex programs running as themselves — the build compiles each demo to a WebAssembly artifact and the page replays the artifact's real stdout frame by frame (looping playback), currently one group, Game of Life, holding three runs: a Gosper glider gun, the acorn, and diehard.
- [Playground](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/playground.html): run and REPL in the browser over the real interpreter compiled to a WebAssembly engine — lazy-loaded behind the open click into a Web Worker, so the page stays responsive while a program runs, with caret diagnostics in both modes, a stdin box, example preloading from the examples page cards, share links carrying source, input, and mode in the URL fragment, and a Stop button in each mode that ends a program that never finishes (a stopped REPL session starts fresh).
- [Advent of Code](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/advent-of-code.html): December 2025's twelve puzzles plus the 2023 and 2024 archive years' 25 days each — one door per day with the puzzle outline and the solution behind a details toggle (a browser run panel on the compiled days), and year tabs. The suites under `aoc/<year>/` run with `bin/zhex test aoc` (the `just aoc` recipe), and the site build re-runs every door that compiles to WebAssembly byte-for-byte against the interpreter; fenced doors are listed with their reason instead.
- [Roadmap](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/roadmap.html): what is done, what is next, and what is future, mirrored by a public project board.
- [Changelog](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/changelog.html): every shipped milestone from the roadmap's Done section, grouped by area and generated from ROADMAP.md.
- [Error catalog](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html): built-in diagnostic codes with their meanings and fixes; application codes from `error.new`/`error.wrap` are not catalog entries. Diagnostics print `file:line:column: message` plus an excerpt, caret, and `hint:` line; `zhex run file.zhex --report=json` emits the machine-readable report `{code, severity, file, line, column, message, hint}`, plus optional additive span_start_column/span_end_column (checker diagnostics with a span, never runtime) and `url` (the code's errors-page address, catalog codes only). The same catalog ships inside the binary: `zhex errors` lists every code with its one-line meaning, `zhex errors <code>` prints the full entry with its learn URL (an unknown code suggests the closest and exits nonzero), and `zhex errors --json` emits the whole catalog as `[{code, text, url}]`.
- [Development insight](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/docs/diagnostics-plan.md): `zhex run file.zhex --trace` streams JSONL step events to stderr — one JSON object per line, emitted before any diagnostic, and combinable with `--report=json` (events, then the report). Five events: `{"event":"word-call","word":W,"file":F,"line":N,"args":[...]}`, `{"event":"binding","name":N,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}`, `{"event":"flow-step","word":W,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}`, `{"event":"with-step","word":W,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}` (a with block's step; the value is always its fixed seed), `{"event":"word-return","word":W,"value":V,"file":F,"line":N}`. `word-call` fires only for program words — builtins never emit it; they appear as flow-step or binding effects. Bindings holding a `Result` (a read without postfix `try`) render `ok("inner")` or `err("message")`; other values render per the checker's static types — Int as digits, Bool as `true`/`false`, String verbatim, Unit as the empty string, Buffer as `buffer(<n> lines)`, File as `file("<path>")` — and a `-> Unit` word returns value "". Tracing never fails a run, and output without the flag is unchanged.
- REPL: `zhex repl [--trace]` runs an interactive session where words and values persist across entries; calls use parentheses (`print(1 + 1)`) or the simple comma-separated form (`print 1 + 1`). In a terminal, pending blocks prefill editable indentation; Tab inserts four spaces, Backspace removes one character; four presses dedent one level. An empty or spaces-only continuation line submits, except blank and comment-only lines inside open `()`, `[]`, or `{}`. Closing a completed top-level expression submits it immediately; a pending block still needs a blank line. While editing, Ctrl-C cancels the current entry; Ctrl-D on an empty top-level line exits 0; in a pending entry, an empty or spaces-only continuation line discards the entry and exits. Bracketed paste preserves source indentation. Piped entries retain line-based behavior and need explicit four-space block indentation; tabs and non-ASCII whitespace outside strings or comments remain source errors. An unclosed delimiter at piped EOF is a syntax error. Program `read-line` uses the same terminal reader without source auto-indentation or Tab expansion. Agents can script a session by piping entries to standard input. A blank line ends a multi-line entry when no delimiter is open; a missing indented block or open delimiter continues it. Bare ordinary expressions echo their value; naked Result expressions are rejected and must be handled with `try` or `catch` in the same entry. `words` lists effective parameter, return, and Result signatures sorted by name and shadows a user binding of that name; a word can be redefined with the same effective signature, while an incompatible signature change is rejected transactionally. Parameter inference must resolve within the defining entry. `let` shadows silently. Check and runtime errors print the annotated diagnostic and the session survives; a runtime error keeps the entry's earlier effects. A final input line without a trailing newline still runs. Ctrl-D or the preloaded ordinary REPL word `bye()` exits 0; the zero-argument call form `bye` is equivalent. `bye()` appears in `words`, follows normal redefinition rules, and is unavailable in source files. With `--trace`, the same JSONL step events as `zhex run` stream to stderr with `"file":"repl"`.

- [Standard library direction](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/docs/standard-library.html): current library boundaries and proposed growth. The [complete 129-name inventory and comparative research](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/docs/standard-library-plan.md) distinguishes shipped operations from unimplemented draft stories; do not generate programs using proposed APIs.

## Error codes

Every built-in diagnostic code with its one-line meaning and its learn URL, one line per code — the same catalog the [error catalog](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html) renders and `zhex errors <code>` prints offline. The list between the markers below is generated from internal/lang/catalog.md (`go generate ./internal/lang` regenerates it; never hand-edit), and the same catalog ships as the repository's generated agent skill [skills/diagnostics/SKILL.md](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/skills/diagnostics/SKILL.md).

<!-- zhex:error-codes begin -->
- [addition-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#addition-type): `+` adds two `Int`s, concatenates two `String`s, or concatenates a `String` and an `Int` — the string-context Int exception.
- [argument-count](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#argument-count): A word call passed the wrong number of arguments.
- [argument-missing](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#argument-missing): `console.arg` received an index outside the program's command-line arguments.
- [argument-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#argument-type): An argument's type does not match the parameter.
- [arithmetic-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#arithmetic-type): `- * / %` need `Int` operands.
- [array-range](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#array-range): An array coordinate is outside its dimension.
- [array-rank](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#array-rank): An array shape or index has the wrong rank.
- [array-shape](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#array-shape): An array extent is negative.
- [assignment-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#assignment-type): A binding annotation must match its value's type.
- [bool-operand](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#bool-operand): `and`/`or` need `Bool` on both sides.
- [branch-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#branch-type): The branches of an `if` or the cases of a `match` end in different types where the value is read.
- [buffer-range](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#buffer-range): `buffer.line` or `buffer.set-line` received an index outside the buffer's lines.
- [collection-iterating](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#collection-iterating): An active iteration prevents mutation of the traversed collection.
- [collection-limit](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#collection-limit): A list or array would exceed the runtime limit of 1,000,000 elements.
- [compare-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#compare-type): Equality comparison needs matching `Int`, `Bool`, or `String` values.
- [condition-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#condition-type): An `if` condition must be `Bool`.
- [console-exit-status](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#console-exit-status): `console.exit` requires a status from 0 through 255.
- [console-input](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#console-input): Reading a line from the input stream failed, usually because the input ended.
- [console-output](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#console-output): Writing to the output stream failed.
- [console-utf8](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#console-utf8): The line read from the input stream is not valid UTF-8.
- [date-parse](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#date-parse): A date string is invalid.
- [depth-limit](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#depth-limit): Word recursion passed the runtime depth limit of 256.
- [division-zero](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#division-zero): Division or remainder by zero.
- [doctest-check](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#doctest-check): A `## >` example's expression failed to check or evaluate by itself.
- [doctest-mismatch](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#doctest-mismatch): A `## >` example in a word's doc produced a different value than the expected output lines after it (they run until a blank doc line or the next `## >` line).
- [duplicate-name](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#duplicate-name): This name is already defined in the same scope.
- [duplicate-word](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#duplicate-word): A word with this name already exists, or it collides with a host word.
- [duration-parse](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#duration-parse): A duration string is invalid or outside the supported nanosecond range.
- [empty-block](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#empty-block): A block header is followed by nothing.
- [env-parse](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#env-parse): A line of the file given to `env.load` is not a KEY=VALUE assignment: the `=` is missing, the key is empty, or the key contains spaces.
- [env-read](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#env-read): `env.load` could not read the file: it is missing, or the process may not read it.
- [error-no-cause](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#error-no-cause): `error.cause` was called for an Error without a cause.
- [expected-expression](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#expected-expression): A token cannot start an expression where one is required.
- [expected-indent](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#expected-indent): A construct needs an indented block on the following lines.
- [expected-name](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#expected-name): A keyword appears where a name is required.
- [expected-token](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#expected-token): The parser expected a specific token and found something else.
- [file-bytes-range](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-bytes-range): `file.write-bytes` received a byte value outside 0 through 255; the message names the first offending value.
- [file-delete](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-delete): `file.delete` could not delete the path: it is missing, it is a nonempty folder (the safety default removes a file or an empty folder only; `file.delete-folder(recursive: true)` removes a tree), or the process may not remove it.
- [file-delete-folder](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-delete-folder): `file.delete-folder` could not remove the folder: it holds entries while `recursive` is false (the default removes an empty folder only; pass `recursive: true` for the whole tree), or the process may not remove something inside it.
- [file-exists](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-exists): `file.exists` could not answer for the path: the message names the path and the operating system's reason, and the failure carries the not-found/permission-denied/other taxonomy in its details.
- [file-free-space](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-free-space): `file.free-space` could not report the bytes available on the volume containing the path: the path does not exist, or the platform cannot answer for it.
- [file-list](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-list): `file.list` could not list the folder: the folder is missing, or the process may not read it, or the path is a file.
- [file-make-folder](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-make-folder): `file.make-folder` could not create the folder: a parent is missing (pass `parents: true` to create ancestors), or the target already exists (the default one-level form refuses it; `parents: true` tolerates an existing folder), or the process may not write the parent.
- [file-move](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-move): `file.move` could not rename the source to the target: the source is missing, the target exists (pass `overwrite: true` to replace an existing file), the target is a folder (never replaced in either mode), the two paths are on different devices (no copy fallback), or the process may not rename.
- [file-open](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-open): `file.open`, `file.read`, or a `file.stream` loop could not open the path.
- [file-read](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-read): A read from an open file failed: the stream was drained ("end of file") or the file was closed.
- [file-size](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-size): `file.size` could not get the size of the path: it is missing, or the process may not stat it.
- [file-utf8](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-utf8): A file's content is not valid UTF-8.
- [file-write](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#file-write): `file.write` could not open, write, or close the path; the message names the path, the failing phase, and the operating system's reason.
- [flow-step](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#flow-step): A `flow` block needs at least one step word.
- [immutable-name](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#immutable-name): A name defined with `let` cannot be reassigned.
- [indentation](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#indentation): A line's indent is not a multiple of four spaces, or it opens more than one level at once.
- [instant-parse](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#instant-parse): An instant string is invalid.
- [int-shift-count](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#int-shift-count): A shift word's count is negative.
- [int-shift-width](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#int-shift-width): A shift count of 64 or more in a build whose Int is 64 bits wide: compiled WebAssembly and the browser engine.
- [integer-literal-range](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#integer-literal-range): An integer literal is outside the signed 128-bit range.
- [integer-overflow](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#integer-overflow): An arithmetic result does not fit in a signed 128-bit integer.
- [json-depth](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#json-depth): JSON nesting exceeds the supported depth of 256.
- [json-field](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#json-field): A JSON object has an unknown, duplicate, or missing required field.
- [json-range](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#json-range): A JSON integer or collection exceeds the supported range.
- [json-syntax](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#json-syntax): JSON text is invalid or contains more than one value.
- [json-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#json-type): A JSON value does not match the expected Zhex type.
- [list-range](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#list-range): The list index is negative or outside its current length, or the list is empty where `list.first`, `list.last`, or `list.pop` needs an element.
- [main-parameters](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#main-parameters): A file whose top level has no statements names `word main` as its entry point, and `zhex run` and `zhex compile` call it with no arguments.
- [module-body](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#module-body): An imported file contains top-level statements.
- [nesting-limit](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#nesting-limit): Expressions or blocks nest past the parser's limit.
- [not-available-in-build](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#not-available-in-build): The build that ran the program does not provide this construct.
- [operand-types](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#operand-types): A binary operator got two different operand types.
- [ordering-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#ordering-type): Ordering comparison (`< <= > >=`) needs `Int` operands.
- [print-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#print-type): `print` accepts one `Int`, `String`, or `Bool` value.
- [private-use](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#private-use): A word or record type beginning with an underscore is private to its module.
- [range-context](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#range-context): `range` and `file.stream` exist only inside a `for` loop header — `for n in range(start, end)` and `for line in file.stream(path)`.
- [range-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#range-type): The bounds of `range(start, end)` must both be `Int`; the path of `file.stream(path)` must be `String`.
- [replace-empty](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#replace-empty): `text.replace` was called with an empty old text.
- [source-utf8](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#source-utf8): The file is not valid UTF-8.
- [stack-range](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#stack-range): The stack is empty where `stack.pop`, `stack.peek`, `stack.dup`, or `stack.drop` needs the top element, or has fewer than two elements where `stack.swap` needs the top pair.
- [string-escape](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#string-escape): A string contains an escape Zhex does not support, or invalid UTF-8.
- [tab-character](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#tab-character): A tab appeared outside a string.
- [temporal-invalid](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#temporal-invalid): Numeric date or time components are outside their valid range.
- [temporal-range](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#temporal-range): Temporal arithmetic produced a value outside the supported range.
- [test-failed](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#test-failed): A `.test.zhex` file run by `zhex test` exited nonzero without a diagnostic of its own — a failed `test.check` label, a deliberate exit, or a crash.
- [text-code-point](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#text-code-point): `text.from-code-points` received a code point that is not valid Unicode: negative, above U+10FFFF, or a surrogate half (U+D800..U+DFFF).
- [text-pad-fill](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#text-pad-fill): `text.pad-left` or `text.pad-right` received a fill that is not exactly one code point.
- [text-pad-width](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#text-pad-width): `text.pad-left` or `text.pad-right` received a negative width.
- [text-repeat-count](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#text-repeat-count): `text.repeat` received a negative count.
- [text-to-int](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#text-to-int): The text given to `text.to-int` is not a signed 128-bit decimal integer.
- [time-parse](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#time-parse): A time string is invalid.
- [timezone-load](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#timezone-load): A named time zone is invalid or unavailable.
- [try-input](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#try-input): Postfix `try` and `catch` need a `Result` value to unwrap.
- [unary-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#unary-type): The unary operator (`-`, `not`) received the wrong type.
- [unclosed-delimiter](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#unclosed-delimiter): An opening parenthesis, bracket, or brace has no matching closing delimiter.
- [unexpected-character](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#unexpected-character): A character cannot start any token.
- [unhandled-result](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#unhandled-result): Handle or propagate each Result with `catch` or `try`.
- [unknown-name](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#unknown-name): No binding or word has this name.
- [unknown-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#unknown-type): A type name is not one of `Int`, `Bool`, `String`, `Unit`, `Buffer`, or `File`.
- [unknown-word](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#unknown-word): No word with this name exists.
- [unsupported-code](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#unsupported-code): An internal invariant failed: the checker approved something the evaluator cannot run.
- [unterminated-string](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#unterminated-string): A string literal has no closing quote before the end of the line.
- [use-cycle](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#use-cycle): Modules import each other in a circle; the message spells the files in the cycle.
- [use-location](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#use-location): A `use` appears inside a word body or another block.
- [use-missing](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#use-missing): A `use` names a module that could not be loaded.
- [use-reserved](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#use-reserved): A module is named `text`, `int`, `buffer`, `file`, or `console`.
- [with-location](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#with-location): A `with` line did not directly follow the expression line it continues.
- [with-seed](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#with-seed): A `with` block's seed produces Unit, so no step can receive it.
- [with-step](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#with-step): A `with` step name resolved neither through the block's namespace nor as a word in scope.
- [word-result](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#word-result): The word's final statement produces a different type than its declared result.
- [xml-depth](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#xml-depth): XML nesting exceeds the supported depth of 256.
- [xml-field](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#xml-field): An XML element or attribute name is unknown, duplicated, missing, collides with its counterpart, or is namespace-qualified.
- [xml-range](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#xml-range): An XML integer or document exceeds the supported range.
- [xml-syntax](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#xml-syntax): XML text is invalid, carries a DTD or entity declaration, uses an undefined entity, or has more than one root element.
- [xml-type](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/errors.html#xml-type): An XML element or attribute does not match the expected Zhex type, or mixes text with child elements.
<!-- zhex:error-codes end -->

## Reference

- [Language contract](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/docs/initial-language.md): the authoritative syntax and semantics the interpreter enforces.
- [Versioning policy](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/docs/versioning.md): no version numbers anywhere until the standard library's 0.1 release (main-only, no tags, no CHANGELOG before that); from 0.1, 0.x semver — MINOR for breaking changes, PATCH for additions — with git tags per release and a hand-written CHANGELOG.md; no release automation before 0.1.
- [Agent guide](https://github.com/desireco/zhex/blob/main/AGENTS.md): rules for writing correct Zhex and verifying changes with the executable test suite.
- [Example sources](https://desireco.github.io/zhex/examples/hello.zhex): downloadable `.zhex` files — swap the filename for fizzbuzz, fibonacci, gcd, times-table, factorial, palindrome, composition, with-blocks, calls, partials, records, choices, collections, maps, json-config, json-tree, xml-config, word-defaults, temporal, life, edit-distance, collatz, text-stats, line-filter, score-report, sorting, file-write, paths, file-work, env-config, recovery, or exit-status; the two-file module programs live at examples/modules/main.zhex with its math.zhex beside it and examples/modules/md-report/main.zhex with its md.zhex beside it, and the html composition module pairs the same way at examples/modules/html-page/main.zhex with its html.zhex (`html.escape-text`, `html.attr`, `html.element`, `html.page`, `html.raw` — escaped unless raw; `html.link` rejects any scheme besides relative, http, https, and mailto); the epub-book program assembles at examples/modules/epub-book/main.zhex with its epub.zhex and zip.zhex beside it (epub.test.zhex and zip.test.zhex pin the archive laws), the pdf writer at examples/modules/pdf-doc/main.zhex with its pdf.zhex beside it (pdf.test.zhex pins the document bytes), the diff module at examples/modules/text-diff/main.zhex with its diff.zhex beside it (diff.test.zhex pins the patch law), and the writer showcase at examples/modules/writer/main.zhex with its co-located md.zhex beside it (writer.test.zhex pins the passes and edits); the module tests live at examples/modules/math.test.zhex with math.zhex and test.zhex beside it (`test.check(condition, label)` fails the run with its label when the condition is false; `zhex test [path]` runs every `*.test.zhex` file as its own process plus every other `.zhex` file's doctests, and `zhex test --gaps` lists public words referenced by no doctest and no test file).
- [Project board](https://github.com/users/desireco/projects/8): the backlog and delivered work as issues on a public Kanban board.
